questions.text: What is the register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: The map in registers.map: ID 0x00, ENABLE 0x04, PERIOD_REQ 0x08, PERIOD_EFF 0x0C, STATUS 0x10, FRAMES 0x14, OVERRUNS 0x18, COUNTER 0x1C, TAKE 0x20, TICK 0x24, 32-bit words.
questions.reason: The request names the registers but gives no offsets, so the map is a proposal.
questions.answer:
FRAMES: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames that fell due and were held, wrapping
STAT: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: [0] a frame waits, [1] enabled
OVERRUNS: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames dropped because one was waiting, wrapping
REQ: offset 0x01, RW, reset 100: [15:0] period asked for, as written
TICK: offset 0x03, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks, one per clock; reads 0
CTRL: offset 0x00, RW, reset 0: [0] enable
CNT: offset 0x08, RO, reset 0: [15:0] ticks counted towards the next frame
TAKE: offset 0x04, WO, reset 0: any write takes the waiting frame; reads 0
EFF: offset 0x02, RO, reset 100: [15:0] period in force
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: unlisted offsets: read 0, writes dropped; read-only registers also drop writes
questions.evidence: FRAMES: offset 0x06, RO, reset 0: [15:0] frames that fell due and were held, wrapping

questions.text: What does the counter read after switching off?
questions.default: It keeps its last value and restarts from zero on the next switch on.
questions.reason: The request says switching off stops counting and says nothing about clearing the counter.
questions.answer: CNT reads 0 after switch-off. The switch-off clears the counter, so the proposed default (keeps its last value) is not what the spec says.
questions.evidence: Switch-on (0 to 1) clears CNT and loads EFF from the request; switch-off clears CNT and the waiting frame; totals persist until reset; writing 1 while on does nothing.

questions.text: What happens when TAKE and a newly due frame fall in the same clock?
questions.default: The take is applied first and the new frame is held.
questions.reason: This is the case where no frame is lost and the request leaves it open.
questions.answer: The take is applied first and the new frame is held.

questions.text: Does PERIOD_EFF change at once when PERIOD_REQ is written while enabled?
questions.default: PERIOD_EFF shows the value in force for the current count, so it changes only at the next wrap or switch on.
questions.reason: The request says the period in force is the one used for counting.
questions.answer: No. EFF does not change when REQ is written while enabled. A new request applies from the next count (wrap) or the switch-on, so EFF changes only at the next wrap or switch-on. The proposed default's conclusion matches the spec, though the spec's register is named EFF, not PERIOD_EFF.
questions.evidence: a new request applies from the next count or the switch-on

questions.text: What are the values of TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?
questions.reason: The request names the parameters but gives no values.
questions.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000, not 1000000 as proposed. BUILD_STAMP is not specified, so the proposed default of 0 is not supported.

questions.text: Is writing ENABLE = 1 while already enabled a restart of the count?
questions.default: No, it does nothing while already on, and only a 0 to 1 change restarts the count.
questions.reason: The request says switching on starts counting, which implies a change of state.
questions.answer: No. Writing 1 while already enabled does nothing and does not restart the count. Only a 0 to 1 switch-on clears CNT.
questions.evidence: Switch-on (0 to 1) clears CNT and loads EFF from the request; switch-off clears CNT and the waiting frame; totals persist until reset; writing 1 while on does nothing.
